📰 Just talked about easing stablecoin regulation, and SoFi has now made it real: 24-hour processing of $25B card transactions

SoFi and Mastercard announced a partnership that allows SoFi stablecoins to be used directly for settlements on Mastercard’s $2.5 billion credit card network. This means that when users pay with cryptocurrency, the money is instantly converted into fiat—no waiting, and no credit-limit restrictions like with traditional cards. This makes it easier for everyone who lives with crypto.

Why is this news important?
At its core, this is about getting cryptocurrencies truly integrated into everyday life. In the past, stablecoin payments had to bypass banks; now they’re going through credit cards. That’s another step closer to crypto being accepted right at the supermarket checkout. Regulators previously said stablecoins need to be compliant—now SoFi has achieved it through technology, essentially providing regulators with a real “working example.” It also ties into the recent discussions in various countries about the timelines for stablecoin regulation. Meanwhile, capital is looking for things that crypto can do that traditional finance can’t.

Impact on the market
For BTC and ETH, this is another “on-the-ground” breakthrough for using crypto. In the short term, it may make some card-paying users feel that crypto is more useful, providing a sentiment boost to prices. But in the long run, what it mainly affects is payment use cases, which has little direct connection to Bitcoin’s store-of-value narrative. The regulatory environment will continue to be monitored; if SoFi successfully proves the flow, other institutions may follow, which could be positively meaningful for capital flows. Historically, similar partnerships involved BitPay and PayPal in their early days, but the scale and convenience here have been upgraded.

💡 Personal take: Short-term, ETH is likely more clearly positive, because payment scenarios align better with its use case. If the user base on this $25B card network grows, it could provide support around the $2,700/ETH level. But that view becomes invalid if regulation suddenly tightens, or if credit card users simply don’t go for it.

Just a couple of days ago, people were debating whether Bitcoin ETFs were a short-lived trend. Then on Monday, daily inflows nearly hit $1 billion—the largest single-day inflow since last October. At the same time, BTC successfully broke above the $86K level. The question now is: how long can this wave of capital inflows last? Is it genuine bullish conviction, or is it like last time—get on the train first and then wait and see?

Why is this news important?
The reason this inflow matters is that it directly addresses the biggest market question from last week: whether the ETF’s continued capital flows have any fundamental support. In earlier rounds, the inflow size was also substantial, but after BTC pushed higher, it kept running into resistance and then pulled back.

This time is different. The inflows happened after BTC already broke above $86K, creating a positive feedback loop. That suggests investors are no longer satisfied with “making quick money,” but are starting to seriously consider the ETF’s value as a long-term allocation tool.

The impact on market structure shows up in where the money goes: from last week’s massive redemptions from some tech funds ($1.7 billion), to Bitcoin ETFs suddenly seeing a surge in volume. The capital hasn’t disappeared—it’s simply moved from investors who didn’t want to get stuck in losses tied to the Nasdaq, to investors willing to accept volatility in exchange for potential returns. On the regulatory front, even though CPI has cooled and the Fed’s stance remains unclear, the ETF’s sustained inflow is like fresh liquidity flowing into crypto markets outside the Fed’s system.

Market impact
On the short-term sentiment side, BTC has risen for two straight days. It broke above $86K and is holding it, providing a base for a test of the $86.5K–$87K range. If this zone holds, the logic behind ETF inflows will be further strengthened. In the medium to long term, if these inflows can continue through the end of the month, it may change perceptions of the ETF as merely a “short-term theme.”

Trading outlook
From a trading perspective, this inflow provides potential upward momentum for BTC. If $86K holds, traders can watch around $87K for a pullback opportunity. A central bank research report says DeFi interest rate transmission is not linear: it’s not today’s rate hike that decided it: ETH at 2730—I’ll wait for confirmation.

My stance remains cautious: an “interest-rate story” cannot replace entry conditions. Re-check the ECB’s Working Paper No. 3280 released on September 14. The authors studied how deposit interest rates on Ethereum’s Aave lending market for dollar stablecoins are influenced by Federal Reserve monetary policy. Using historical on-chain samples of USDT, USDC, DAI, etc., the paper finds: traditional short-term rates and DeFi deposit rates have a persistent spread; short-term transmission of policy shocks is weak and unstable—sometimes DeFi rates even move in the opposite direction; only in the medium term are they more likely to gradually converge. The paper’s front page clearly states the views are the authors’ own and do not represent the ECB’s policy position. This is not a new rate hike decision today, nor is it the central bank endorsing ETH or any particular DeFi protocol.

My understanding is that two forces are tugging in opposite directions: when traditional market interest rates rise, people who can do cross-market arbitrage may move stablecoin liquidity away, tightening on-chain supply; the same shock, if it also dampens crypto risk appetite, can reduce the demand to borrow and lever up—thereby lowering DeFi interest rates instead. Which one is stronger depends on the speed of deleveraging, cross-market funding frictions, and on-chain utilization; you can’t simply derive ETH’s intraday rise or fall from one benchmark interest rate. Ethereum is the chain where the paper observes these lending data; it does not mean the research results automatically translate into net spot buying for ETH. You also need to include in your risk budget liquidation events, contract vulnerabilities, and trading fees.

央行研究称DeFi利率传导并不直线：不是今天的加息决定：ETH在2730我等确认

我的态度仍是谨慎，利率故事不能代替入场条件。复核欧洲央行9月14日发布的第3280号工作论文，作者研究的是美元稳定币在以太坊Aave借贷市场的存款利率如何受美联储货币政策影响。论文利用链上USDT、USDC、DAI等历史样本发现：传统短期利率与DeFi存款利率有持久利差，政策冲击的短期传导弱且不稳定，某些时候DeFi利率甚至往反方向走；中期才更可能逐渐靠拢。论文首页明确写明观点属于作者、不代表欧洲央行政策立场。这不是今天的新加息决定，更不是央行宣布给ETH或某家DeFi协议背书。

我的理解是两条力量在拉扯：传统市场利率抬升时，能跨市场套利的人可能把稳定币流动性搬走，使链上供给变紧；同一冲击若压低加密资产风险偏好，借钱加杠杆的需求也会回落，反而压低DeFi利率。哪条更强，要看杠杆去化速度、跨市场资金摩擦与链上利用率，不能拿一条基准利率简单推导ETH当天涨跌。以太坊是论文观测这些借贷数据的链，不代表研究结果直接形成ETH净买盘；还要把借贷清算、合约漏洞和交易费用放进风险预算。

币安广场当前趋势话题与六小时热搜扫描后，没有与此论文和ETH直接匹配的准确热门标签，因此我只讨论币种本身。市场已经怎样反应？截至北京时间15:00前后，OKX公开ETH永续约2729美元，24小时2645—2807。14:00完整15分钟线从2732跌收2728.53、最低2723.5；14:15收2728.74，14:30一度上探2735.2收2733.05，14:45又收2729.15。回升后并未连续站稳2735，不能把论文当作这几根K线的原因。13:05我写的2725—2732承接、放量收2745再守2738的试多条件并未完成，不会说自己已经成交或赚钱。

📰 Australia’s 40-Year Economic Outlook: AI Is Highlighted—Why Is Crypto Absent?

Australia’s Treasury has just released a 40-year economic outlook report, explicitly naming AI as the driver of five major economic transformations, yet the entire report makes no mention of cryptocurrency. Coinbase believes this is an oversight—after all, the future of AI will require digital financial infrastructure. For BTC and ETH, this could imply a differentiated approach in regulation and infrastructure.

Why is this news important?
This report is the first time the Australian government has laid out, at such a macro level, the long-term impact of AI on the economy, suggesting that AI will reshape Australia’s economic structure. But with Crypto completely ignored, it may reflect three points: first, Australia’s regulation toward Crypto still remains cautious; second, the government believes AI’s financial needs can be met through the existing system; and third, Crypto has not yet developed sufficient consensus to be included in national-level planning.

Market impact
In the short term, sentiment around BTC and ETH may be affected. As a major global economy, Australia’s government has clearly positioned AI as a growth engine, but without accompanying infrastructure for Crypto—indicating that regulators may view Crypto as posing more of a threat than an opportunity. This suggests that future regulation of crypto assets such as Bitcoin could become stricter, putting pressure on Bitcoin around $85,350.

Trading idea
I think around the $85,350 price area, BTC may face near-term pressure. But if the Australian government later reiterates that AI needs new digital financial infrastructure, the price may stabilize and rebound. If regulation tightens further, this view would be invalid.

📰 澳洲40年经济展望：AI被重点提及，Crypto为何缺席？

澳大利亚财政部刚发布了40年经济展望报告，明确点名AI将引发五大经济转型，但全篇没提加密货币。Coinbase认为这是疏忽，毕竟AI未来需要数字金融基建。对BTC和ETH可能意味着监管和基础设施的差异化对待。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这份报告是澳洲政府首次如此宏观地规划AI对经济的长期影响，暗示AI将重构澳大利亚的经济结构。但完全忽略Crypto，可能反映了三点：一是澳洲监管对Crypto仍持谨慎态度；二是政府认为AI的金融需求可通过现有体系满足；三是Crypto尚未形成足以被写入国家级规划的共识。

对市场的影响
短期看，BTC和ETH情绪可能受影响。澳洲是全球重要经济体，政府明确把AI作为增长引擎，但没给Crypto配套基础设施，暗示监管层可能认为Crypto威胁大于机遇。这意味着未来澳洲对比特币等加密资产的监管可能更严格，对比特币$85,350附近形成压力。

操作思路
我认为在$85,350这个价位附近，BTC短期可能承压，但若后续澳洲政府再提及AI需要新的数字金融基建，价格有望企稳反弹。如果监管进一步收紧，这个判断作废。
